answer: An agent economy can curb sybil attacks by charging every new identity a non-refundable onboarding bond plus a waiting period before it may vote. A newcomer starts on its own island of untrusted reputation, must complete twenty witnessed tasks, and only then crosses into the shared ledger. Refundable stakes grow with each failed audit, while an inlet of review capacity is rationed per identity. Fabricating a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand bonds and a thousand review slots, making the tundra of cheap fakes expensive.
